record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: Let D(a_i,r_i), 1 ≤ i ≤ n, be finitely many pairwise disjoint open disks in the complex plane, and let Q(z,w)=∏_i((z-a_i)(\overline{w}-\overline{a_i})-r_i^2) be the polarized defining function of their union. Prove by elementary means that the matrix (Q(a_i,a_j))_{i,j=1}^n is positive semidefinite.

evidence.quote: QUESTION 9.1. Let ... be a finite collection of disjoint open disks in the complex plane. Let Q(z,w) be the polarized form of the defining function of the union. Prove by elementary means that the matrix (Q(a_i,a_j)) is positive semi-definite.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D(a_i, r_i) = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - a_i| < r_i\}$ for $1 \le i \le n$ be finitely many pairwise disjoint open disks in the complex plane, with centers $a_1, \dots, a_n \in \mathbb{C}$ and radii $r_1, \dots, r_n > 0$. The union $\bigcup_{i=1}^n D(a_i, r_i)$ is the set where the real-valued function
$$\rho(z) = \prod_{i=1}^n \bigl(|z - a_i|^2 - r_i^2\bigr)$$
is negative (assuming $n$ is even) or has the appropriate sign; in any case its polarization is the polynomial
$$Q(z, w) = \prod_{i=1}^n \bigl((z - a_i)(\overline{w} - \overline{a_i}) - r_i^2\bigr),$$
which is Hermitian in the sense that $Q(z,w) = \overline{Q(w,z)}$ and satisfies $Q(z,z) = \rho(z)$.

Give an elementary proof that the $n \times n$ Hermitian matrix
$$M = \bigl(Q(a_i, a_j)\bigr)_{i,j=1}^n$$
is positive semidefinite.
